In ice_misc_intr_thread_fn()
column2: if we do not complete all Tx timestamp work

column1: the thread function will poll continuously forever.
For E822 hardware
column2: this wastes time as the return value from

column1: ice_ptp_process_ts() is accurate and always reports correctly that the PHY
actually has new timestamp data.
In addition
column2: if we receive enough timestamps with the right pacing

column1: never exit this polling. Should this occur
ice_misc_intr_thread_fn() will never be processed.
Fix this by instead writing to PFINT_OICR
be triggered immediately. This does take slightly more processing than just
re-checking the timestamps. However
column2: it allows all of the other interrupt

column1: causes a chance to be processed first in the hard IRQ function.
Note that the OICR interrupt is configured to be throttled  to no more than
once every 124 microseconds. This gives an effective interrupt rate of
~8000 interrupts per second. This should thus not cause a significant
increase in overall CPU usage when compared to sleeping.
